title: Estimation and Tracking of Blood Pressure Using Routinely Acquired Photoplethysmographic Signals and Deep Neural Networks
summary: A Siamese deep network estimated blood-pressure changes from PPG after one calibration reading, using 329 MIMIC-II patients and patient-disjoint held-out evaluation. This is retrospective ICU-waveform feasibility evidence, not prospective care validation.
ai_technology: A Siamese deep neural network estimates blood-pressure changes from PPG using one calibration reading.
organization: Signal and Image Processing Laboratory (SIPL), Andrew and Erna Viterbi Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Technion - Israel Institute of Technology, Haifa, Israel

evidence.tested: Siamese deep network estimates blood-pressure changes from PPG relative to one calibration reading; 329 MIMIC-II patients and patient-disjoint held-out split. Retrospective ICU waveform feasibility, not prospective care validation.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective MIMIC-II data and a held-out split do not establish prospective bedside performance or patient benefit.
evidence.ai_role: A Siamese deep neural network estimates blood-pressure changes from PPG using one calibration reading.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
